findings.claim: The hospitality and catering industry is one of the largest sectors in the UK economy, employing around 2.9 million people and generating £130 billion in economic activity. It is the third-largest private sector employer.
findings.truth: UKHospitality currently gives 3.5 million workers and a £93 billion direct annual economic contribution; it calls hospitality the UK's third-largest employer.

findings.claim: Personal service delivers food directly to an individual, wherever they are.
findings.truth: The specification lists takeaway under personal service even though the customer collects it. Either define personal service as provision to an individual that includes delivery and collection, or reclassify takeaway. The first option retains the specification's categories but requires consistent changes across the definition, content, conclusion, glossary and flashcards.

findings.claim: The kitchen brigade hierarchy (top to bottom): Executive Chef → Sous Chef → Chef de Partie → Commis Chef → Pastry Chef → Kitchen Assistant → Apprentice → Kitchen Porter / Plongeur.
findings.truth: The specification lists these as roles, not as one rank order. A pastry chef is a specialist/station role, while kitchen porters and plongeurs are support roles; they should not be taught as consecutive positions below a commis chef.
findings.evidence: spec 1.1.2; Culinary Institute of America, Kitchen Brigade Explained (fetched 2026-09-04)

findings.claim: Food hygiene certificates are essential for all kitchen staff.
findings.truth: Food handlers need adequate supervision, instruction and/or training for their work; a food hygiene certificate is not a legal requirement.
findings.evidence: Food Standards Agency, Food hygiene training record (fetched 2026-09-04)

findings.claim: Full-time workers are entitled to a minimum of 28 days including bank holidays.
findings.truth: The statutory minimum is 5.6 weeks. It is 28 days for a worker on a five-day week and bank holidays may be included.

findings.claim: A restaurant must label dishes with allergen symbols.
findings.truth: Restaurants must provide information about the 14 regulated allergens, but may choose how to provide it. Symbols are one option, not a legal requirement.
findings.evidence: Food Standards Agency, Allergen guidance for food businesses (fetched 2026-09-04)

findings.claim: RIDDOR reportable incidents include major injuries and burns requiring hospital treatment, and all reports must be made without delay.
findings.truth: RIDDOR uses specified injuries and specified dangerous occurrences. Deaths, specified injuries and dangerous occurrences require notification without delay; an over-seven-day injury must be reported within 15 days.
findings.evidence: HSE, Specified reportable injuries; HSE, When do I need to report an incident? (fetched 2026-09-04)

findings.claim: Gluten intolerance (coeliac disease) — the body cannot digest gluten.
findings.truth: Coeliac disease is an autoimmune condition: gluten triggers an immune reaction that damages the small intestine. It is not an inability to digest gluten or simply a food intolerance.

findings.claim: A food hygiene rating must be displayed at the premises.
findings.truth: Display is compulsory in Wales and Northern Ireland, but not in England; ratings are searchable online across all three nations.
findings.evidence: Food Standards Agency, FHRS Display Audit 2022 (fetched 2026-09-04)

findings.claim: The danger zone is 5°C to 63°C and food must reach a core temperature of at least 75°C.
findings.truth: FSA consumer guidance defines the danger zone as 8°C to 63°C and gives time-temperature combinations for cooking, including 70°C for 2 minutes or 75°C for 30 seconds. Option A: update every temperature reference to that guidance. Option B: retain 5°C only as a fridge operating target and distinguish it from the 8°C danger-zone threshold. This would ripple through content, conclusion, exam tip, practice material and flashcards.
findings.evidence: Food Standards Agency, Cooking your food (fetched 2026-09-04)

summary: Ten lessons were checked against the Unit 1 specification and fetched authoritative sources. Eight verified findings have surgical edits; two broader consistency corrections need editorial adjudication.
